notes: Arduino Nano Matter is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type with Nano-style pin names (D0-D12, A0-A7, 3V3, 5V, GND).
The tutorial text says the driver is powered from 3.3V and the fan speed is a PWM signal on D4. The wiring diagram image was not available in the provided material.

The photo shows a Grove cable and a green Grove breakout board between the Nano and the driver. I replaced these with three jumper wires straight to the driver ports, since neither part is in the catalogue.
Which driver pin gets the D4 PWM signal is not stated. I assumed SCL, the yellow Grove wire. This is a guess.
Breadboard hole positions for the Nano pins are assumed. The Nano straddles the centre gap, with 3V3 on one side and D4 and GND on the other.
The motor leads connect directly to MOTOR_OUT1 and MOTOR_OUT2 (the photo shows red and black leads going to the driver).

The validator still flags five edges: wire-end to pin on the driver for VCC, GND and SCL, and lead to screw for the two motor leads. This is a mismatch in the catalogue's port kinds for the motor-driver-grove-i2c-mini part, not a wiring error. The module has pin and screw-terminal ports, and a jumper wire end or a motor lead does connect to them physically. I kept these edges because the manual requires them, and dropping them would leave the driver and motor disconnected. The first fix attempt removed the 'electrical' edges and the validator then flagged the 'joined' edges instead.
The Google Nest Hub Max and the phone app are the Matter/Thread network side, not part of the wired circuit, so they are left out.
